title: Making markets work: The role of effective public institutions in enabling private sector growth and development
gist: World Bank governance staff summarize the 'Institutions and Prosperity' report, which diagnoses public-institution effectiveness in regulation and procurement along organizational capacity (personnel, budgets, information systems, management) and governance capacity (accountability, independence, transparency). Procurement personnel quality correlates with ease of contracting with government even after controlling for GDP per capita, and regulator accountability varies widely by sector even within the OECD.

themes.theme: Scale of the state in markets

insights.claim: About 400 million of the roughly 3.74 billion people in the global workforce, or 11 percent, work in the public sector.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Sizes the global public-sector labor pool relevant to govtech and services markets.

insights.claim: Public procurement spending in OECD countries averaged 12.7% of GDP.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Public procurement is a huge addressable market whose efficiency affects contractor margins.
insights.quote: in OECD countries public procurement spending as a share of GDP averaged 12.7%

insights.claim: The Institutions and Prosperity report defines institutional capacity along two dimensions: organizational (staff, budgets, systems) and governance (mechanisms ensuring delivery serves the public rather than private or political interests), and argues neither works alone.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Useful lens for assessing country risk in regulated sectors and public contracting.
insights.quote: Both matter, and neither works alone.

insights.claim: A well-trained, well-equipped institution can still fail without independence, and accountability mechanisms cannot compensate for chronically underfunded or undertrained agencies.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Regulatory capture risk persists even in technically competent agencies; check independence, not just capability.
insights.quote: A well-trained staff with strong information systems can still fail if the institution lacks independence.

insights.claim: Organizational capacity has four components: personnel quality and incentives, budget allocation and management, information systems that cut transaction costs, and management practices; personnel quality stands out as especially critical in procurement and regulation.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Civil-service quality is the key variable for predictable regulation and contracting.

insights.claim: Countries with higher-quality procurement staff consistently report greater ease of contracting with government, and the correlation remains significant at the 90 percent level after controlling for GDP per capita.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Procurement staff quality is a measurable predictor of friction for government contractors across EMs.
insights.quote: Countries with higher-quality procurement staff consistently report greater ease in contracting with government

insights.claim: Governance capacity has three mutually reinforcing dimensions: accountability, independence from industry and political pressure, and transparency; transparency has limited value without accountability for poor outcomes.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Framework for judging regulatory capture risk in utilities, telecoms and transport.
insights.quote: transparency has limited value without accountability mechanisms for poor outcomes

insights.claim: Even within the OECD, sector regulators vary considerably in whether they are accountable to the legislature or directly to the public, based on 230 sector regulators in 46 countries across energy, e-communications, rail, air and water.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Regulatory risk must be assessed sector by sector, not country by country.

insights.claim: Strong institutions in one sector do not automatically translate into strong institutions in another sector of the same country.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Country-level governance scores can mislead sector-specific investment decisions.
insights.quote: strong institutions in one sector do not automatically translate to strong institutions in another

insights.claim: The diagnostic framework can extend beyond procurement and regulators to customs, tax administration, central ministries and subnational institutions.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Expect World Bank reform lending targeting customs and tax administration using this lens.
